concepts.name: the valuation: for a prime and a number on my line, the p-adic depth — the p-rung of the first-divisor factorization chain, counting how many times the prime divides before the stop; every recorded number carries its depths as facts

lesson.statement: the valuation, the p-adic depth, read off the first-divisor factorization chain: for a prime p and a number on my line, it is the number of times the p-rung of the chain divides the number before the stop — the highest power of p that divides it — and every recorded number carries each of its depths as a fact, at the line end 84

concepts.name: the lift-the-exponent form: for an odd prime p dividing the difference x minus y and dividing neither term, the p-adic depth of x to the n power minus y to the n power is the p-adic depth of the difference plus the p-adic depth of the exponent — verified in every instance of the line's ledger box

lesson.statement: the lift-the-exponent identity, the classical odd-p form, as the rule i was given: when an odd prime p divides the difference x minus y and divides neither x nor y, the p-adic depth of x to the n power minus y to the n power is the p-adic depth of the difference x minus y plus the p-adic depth of the exponent n — my ledger in the line's box (the odd primes at or below the line end, the difference a multiple of the prime with neither term divisible by it, the exponents three through the line end) verifies every instance of it, at the line end 84

concepts.name: the summit of the island: the statement itself, a declared record fact (the ams beal prize) — with all three exponents above two, a to the x power plus b to the y power equal to c to the z power forces a common prime factor of a, b and c; on my line the verification census carries it and the primitive territory is a wall

lesson.statement: the statement of the island, of record, as the ams beal prize holds it: if a to the x power plus b to the y power equals c to the z power, and a, b, c, x, y and z are positive integers with x, y and z each above two, then a, b and c have a common prime factor — that is, the equation has no solution in pairwise coprime a, b and c once every exponent is above two, at the line end 84

concepts.name: the verification census: in the box where a, b, c lie at or below the line end and the exponents stand between three and ten of record, exactly 83 triples solve the island's equation and every one carries its common prime factor — zero primitive triples on the line; the line ends where the primitive triples would live

lesson.statement: the verification census on my line: in the box where a, b, c lie at or below my line end and the exponents x, y, z stand between three and ten of record, exactly eighty-three triples solve the island's equation, and every one of the eighty-three carries its common prime factor — the two-power twin family, the three-family, the seven-family, the fifteen-family, and the seventeen, nineteen, twenty-six, twenty-eight, thirty-one, thirty-three families — while zero primitive triples live on my line; the line ends where the primitive triples would live, and that territory is a wall, at the line end 84

theorems.statement: the ledger filed on the line: the lift-the-exponent identity, the classical odd-p form, verified in every instance of the ledger's box — the odd primes at or below my line end, the difference a multiple of the prime with neither term divisible by it, the exponents three through the line end — two hundred forty-nine thousand two hundred eighty instances, zero deviations, at the line end 84

the summit of the island filed on my line: the statement holds of record across the whole census box — the eighty-three triples of the box each carry their common prime factor, no primitive triple lives in the box, and the primitive territory is a wall, at the line end 84
